t.15.1: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of the imperishable aśvattha tree with its roots above and its branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.
t.15.2: Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the guṇas, with sense-objects as their shoots; and below, in the world of men, its roots stretch forth, binding through action.
t.15.3: Its form is not perceived here as such, nor its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation; having cut down this aśvattha tree, with its firmly grown roots, by the strong axe of non-attachment,
t.15.4: Then that state must be sought, having gone to which they do not return again: 'I take refuge in that very primal Puruṣa, from whom the ancient activity has streamed forth.'
t.15.5: Free from pride and delusion, having conquered the fault of attachment, ever devoted to the Self, with desires wholly turned away, released from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded go to that imperishable state.
t.15.6: Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire illumines that; having gone there, they do not return. That is my supreme abode.
t.15.7: An eternal portion of Myself alone, having become the living soul in the world of living beings, draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which abide in material nature.
t.15.8: Whatever body the lord obtains, and whatever body he departs from, he goes on taking these with him, as the wind carries scents from their source.
t.15.9: Presiding over the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, and the mind as well, this one enjoys the objects of the senses.
t.15.10: Whether departing, or remaining, or experiencing while joined with the guṇas, the deluded do not perceive him; those who have the eye of knowledge see him.
t.15.11: Striving yogins see him established in the self; but those of unperfected self, lacking discernment, do not see him, even though they strive.
t.15.12: The radiance that, residing in the sun, illumines the whole world, the radiance that is in the moon and that which is in fire, know that radiance to be mine.
t.15.13: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings by My vital energy; and becoming Soma, whose very nature is sap, I nourish all the plants.
t.15.14: Becoming Vaiśvānara, the fire of digestion, I abide in the bodies of living beings, and, joined with prāṇa and apāna, I digest the four kinds of food.
t.15.15: And I am seated in the heart of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal. By all the Vedas it is I alone who am to be known; I am indeed the maker of the Vedānta and the knower of the Vedas.
t.15.16: There are two Puruṣas in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. The perishable is all beings, and the unchanging one is called the imperishable.
t.15.17: But the highest Person is another, declared to be the Supreme Self, the imperishable Lord who, having entered the three worlds, sustains them.
t.15.18: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Veda as Puruṣottama, the Supreme Person.
t.15.19: He who, free from delusion, thus knows me as the Supreme Person, he, knowing all, worships me with his whole being, O Bhārata.
t.15.20: Thus has this most secret teaching been spoken by me, O sinless one. Having understood this, one becomes truly wise and has accomplished all that is to be done, O Bhārata.
